none: Verse translations and heading only; no commentary point appears on this page.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the isolated letters were discussed in al-Baqarah's exegesis and, in his view, are names of a sūrah.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, they are names of a sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the opening as having an omitted inchoative.
rows.anchor: Here the inchoative (mubtadā’) is suppressed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitāb denotes the Book whose advent God promised through His prophets and messengers.
rows.anchor: It refers to the Book whose advent God promised through His prophets and messengers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the pronoun tilka to refer to Alif Lām Rā, so this sūrah comprises verses of the promised Book.
rows.anchor: The implication is that this s ūrah consists of verses of the promised Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence carries both favour and threat.
rows.anchor: This sentence expresses both favour and threat at the same time.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favour is God's revelation of the promised great gift, which people must sincerely believe in and benefit from.
rows.anchor: The favour referred to is that God has revealed the great gift which He had promised to reveal through his prophets and messengers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat warns those who mock and oppose God's Book to consider the wretched fate they invite.
rows.anchor: those who make fun of them instead of giving them due importance and expend their energies in opposing it should think for themselves about the wretched fate they are inviting.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that what God revealed is true reassures the Prophet: the Qur'an's claims are well-argued, soundly reasoned and absolutely true, and will happen.
rows.anchor: is well-argued, soundly reasoned and absolutely true.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for columns is plural of both ʿamūd and ʿimād, and tarawnahā is its attribute.
rows.anchor: is the plural of both

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse directs attention to God's profound power and wisdom: he raised the sky on invisible columns of gravity.
rows.anchor: It has erected this canopy on such columns of gravity that eyes cannot see them.

rows.speaker: idolaters
rows.claim: Against the idolaters' claim that God became aloof after creating the universe, the throne clause means he continues to govern it.
rows.anchor: as the idolaters contended. He is governing it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon's existence shows that everything is under God's control and cannot depart its ordained course.
rows.anchor: The two great signs of the sun and the moon bear witness by their very existence that everything is in God’s control.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon rise and set at specified times without delay.
rows.anchor: The sun and the moon rise and set at specific times without a second’s delay.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs and their explanation show that people have a prescribed lifetime and must then return to meet God.
rows.anchor: so that people are convinced that have a prescribed time of life. After that they have to return to meet God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the heavenly signs, the earth's features testify to God's governance, power, wisdom and oneness for those who reflect.
rows.anchor: After the signs of the sky, this verse directs attention to the signs of the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though seas and mountains differ, springs from mountains show how God's power and wisdom harmonize opposites.
rows.anchor: God, through His power and wisdom, has created such harmony between them that springs have sprouted from mountains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harmony of the natural world rejects self-origination or separate deities and points to one wise, mighty creator.
rows.anchor: Is this a proof of the fact that they have been created out of their own accord and have different deities governing them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harmony among cosmic opposites shows that one being rules the universe rather than rival gods at war.
rows.anchor: The opposing elements of this universe like the sky and the earth, the sun and the moon, the night and the day have such harmony

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairs of every fruit express a comprehensive law: every fruit and seed occurs in pairs, whether people know it or not.
rows.anchor: every single fruit and seed also occurs in pairs, whether human beings know it or not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even wheat is divided into two parts that remain in complete harmony.
rows.anchor: Even the seed of wheat is divided into two parts; however, both are in complete harmony with one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's paired character points to its counterpart, the hereafter, with both together fulfilling their purpose.
rows.anchor: This paired-phenomenon of the universe bears witness that this world also has pair which is the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs also point to divine creativity and the Day of Judgment, but only reflective people see them; the careless do not benefit.
rows.anchor: There are several signs of God’s creativity, governance, power, wisdom, oneness, and the day of judgement in these things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though crops share water, yields, taste and tree growth vary, which shows that a knowledgeable, wise God supervises the universe as sole sovereign.
rows.anchor: crops are watered with the same water but the extent of produce is different; some cultivated lands have more and some have less.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief requires affirming God's attributes and rights, not merely his existence; God does not need anyone's belief.
rows.anchor: it is essential to believe in His attributes and rights as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' neck-yokes represent arrogance, egotism, blind following and stagnation.
rows.anchor: These people have yokes of arrogance, egotism, blind following and stagnation around their necks.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These yokes prevent people from reflecting on the heavenly signs in 13:2 and earthly signs in 13:3-4.
rows.anchor: These yokes neither allow their necks to be raised up so that they can reflect on the signs of the heavens

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This blindness leads them to Hell forever.
rows.anchor: The consequence of this blindness is that they will land in Hell and rot it in forever.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites Yāsīn 36:8 as a parallel image of neck-yokes preventing people from bowing their heads.
rows.anchor: refers to this in the following words:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathulāt is the plural of mathulah and means chastisement or exemplary punishment.
rows.anchor: It means “chastisement and exemplary punishment.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people wait for punishment and calamity before repenting.
rows.anchor: The verse implies that these people await some punishment and calamity before

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they will accept the Prophet's message only after seeing the threatened doom.
rows.anchor: They say that they will only accept the message of the Prophet (sws) if they see the threatened doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound-minded people learn from experience and past nations, whose accounts are being told, but these people ignore the lesson.
rows.anchor: people who have sound intellect learn from others and through their own experience. They should learn this lesson from the several nations of the past

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God graciously gives disbelievers and polytheists time to reform, but each respite has a limit and he then seizes them sternly.
rows.anchor: It is purely God’s grace that in spite of their disbelief and polytheism, He is giving them a long respite so that they mend their ways.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āyah means a sign of punishment, referring to the punishment the people demanded in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: refers to a sign of punishment. This is a reference to the punishment these people were demanding to hasten in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can show a sign; the Prophet must perform his own warning work and disregard their nonsensical demand.
rows.anchor: It is said that only God has the authority to show a sign and not the prophet. He must do his work

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's practice is to warn a nation before punishment; Quraysh have been sent the Prophet as guide, and refusal means punishment.
rows.anchor: before He punishes a nation, He warns and admonishes them. Thus in the case of the Quraysh, He has sent the Prophet (sws) as a guide.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An event's certainty is not undermined by its timing being unknown or unavailable on demand; denying it is foolish.
rows.anchor: If an event is certain to happen but its time of arrival cannot be foretold or cannot be shown on demand, this cannot negate it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pregnancy illustrates the point: wrongdoers are pregnant with misdeeds, whose burden will eventually be delivered.
rows.anchor: The verse cites the example of pregnancy to prove this claim. The wrong doers are pregnant with misdeeds and one day this burden will be delivered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows when this delivery will happen, and human haste cannot change his established practice.
rows.anchor: the time of this delivery is only known to God. Even if people show haste, they cannot change the established practice of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not compare God's knowledge with their own limits: he knows the unknown and manifest, and others know his plans only as much as he reveals.
rows.anchor: His knowledge embraces the known and the unknown. Only He knows His own intentions and schemes and others know about them to the extent He wants to reveal to them.
